approach.method_basis: The Parent is an accepted-feedback evolutionary search with a Gaussian-process ranker in front of the oracle. Each round it draws parents from the better quantiles of a bounded population of the best molecules seen so far, and breeds a surplus pool of fresh candidates by connected-fragment crossover, an optional finishing edit, or successive local graph mutations with bounded retries; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is switched off, canonical identity and duplicate rejection govern admission, and an earlier change in this lineage added a narrow chemistry rule that refuses a candidate introducing a new unusual sulfur environment its own scored parents did not already carry. Every pool is scored by a Gaussian process fitted to the whole task-local accepted archive. Molecules enter that model as integer counts of their radius-two local atom environments hashed into a fixed-width vector, compared by a generalized Tanimoto similarity; scores are standardized by the archive's own mean and spread, with a fixed small observation noise. The model's joint posterior over the pool is then sampled once per batch slot, and the batch is filled by correlated Thompson draws that pick distinct candidates. Nothing about the model is fitted from the data: the similarity law, the noise level and above all the radius-two choice of what counts as a local environment are constants baked into the method.
approach.novelty: Let the task choose how local the model's notion of chemical similarity should be. At every refit the same similarity law is built three times, over radius-one, radius-two and radius-three environment counts, and the one whose exact log marginal likelihood of the accepted scores is highest supplies that batch's model; the inherited radius-two setting stays on the menu and wins ties and numerical failures. Nothing else moves: the same count vocabulary and vector width, the same similarity formula, the same noise, the same normalization, the same correlated allocator, the same breeder and chemistry gates. What is new is the object being chosen. Every covariance experiment this lineage has run so far swapped one fixed law for another fixed law and lost; none of them varied the environment radius, and the earlier attempts to fit anything at all by marginal likelihood tuned the observation noise rather than the representation, on a different, binary-feature model. The sibling running beside this one adds a whole-molecule composition and property channel and keeps radius two fixed, so it widens what the model looks at while this one changes how finely it looks.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent reads every molecule through one fixed lens: radius-two chirality-aware Morgan environment counts in 2048 folded bins, identical on every task and at every refit. Its three summary.json/run.log pairs are complete, with macro mean 0.59645311428869 and population SD 0.03397032998399878; seed macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287 and 0.583088384937917; per-task means deco_hop 0.7069397917343436 (SD 0.10595225525592393), drd2_docking 0.9910169833369453 (SD 0.007432770555240714), median_2 0.22273152064211169 (SD 0.007360172753262417), sitagliptin_mpo 0.6047677442780907 (SD 0.08009460182388871) and zaleplon_mpo 0.4568095314519592 (SD 0.015278237102820594); paired delta against n-62daf219c70a +0.0007834645552323346. Nine fixed substitutions of the similarity law have now lost on this lineage: on this Parent squared -0.044471550095667355 (n-36a7bb9883ec), normalized inner product -0.07722665959076568 (n-52bd6c308406), the coherent fixed exponential law -0.03317204680473033 (n-a11bce06c3f9), mean-only exponential -0.05826897931006499 (n-14a52e3f8725) and residual-only exponential -0.02971005981260903 (n-6ebafca203bf); under n-62daf219c70a min/max -0.04824526182151967 (n-dd2b25d32925), unfolded counts -0.04816296717262832 (n-b14daceabbeb), that same exponential law's ungated precedent -0.032277693549492024 (n-07dd356cb779) and normalized Matern -0.02750824038854201 (n-ea03f38e7e10). Not one of them changed the environment radius: every Morgan fingerprint built in any published source of this campaign uses radius 2, so radius 1 and radius 3 have never been evaluated in any form. The sharpest symptom is the objective the Research Brief names. Parent median_2 endpoints are 0.2145, 0.2214 and 0.2323, and all 24 round-28 sibling cells (n-14a52e3f8725, n-36a7bb9883ec, n-52bd6c308406, n-605c7a785b51, n-6ebafca203bf, n-8df0bb3bbcfe, n-a11bce06c3f9, n-f04cec6ab705) sit inside 0.1918-0.2397 whichever fixed law was installed. A read-only recomputation of the exact log marginal likelihood of this Parent's own accepted archives, at the same 29 refit points per task with the same standardization, noise SD 0.05 and jitter ladder, shows the fixed lens is usually not the one the labels prefer: over all 435 inherited refits radius 2 wins only 91, radius 1 wins 124 and radius 3 wins 220. median_2 prefers radius 1 at 87 of 87 fits, zaleplon_mpo and sitagliptin_mpo prefer radius 3 at 87 of 87 each, drd2_docking starts at radius 3 and moves to radius 2 as the archive grows, and deco_hop splits by seed (27 of 29 fits at radius 1 in seed 0, 27 of 29 at radius 2 in seed 1). The median winning margin is about 25 nats and the smallest is 0.1251, so these are decided preferences rather than near ties. The bottleneck is therefore not which single fixed locality is best; it is that one global locality is imposed where the task's own accepted labels already express different, strong and stable preferences.
hypothesis: At every inherited refit, select the Morgan environment radius of the inherited dot-product count Tanimoto covariance from the menu 1, 2 or 3 over the same chirality-aware 2048-bin folded count vocabulary by the maximum exact log marginal likelihood of the inherited standardized accepted targets under observation noise SD 0.05 and the inherited jitter ladder, preferring the inherited radius 2 on an exact tie or a failed factorization, and use that single selected radius coherently for the training, cross, pool and probe features, the posterior mean and the correlated residual covariance of that batch.

finding_summary.headline: Likelihood-chosen Morgan radius ran exactly as designed but lost 0.040: radius-3 picks weakened ranking, radius 1 helped median_2
finding_summary.insights: Selecting a hyperparameter by marginal likelihood has now twice been exactly activated, slightly improved calibration, weakened within-batch ranking and lost endpoint score. Here the selected quantity was the fingerprint radius; in the earlier test it was the observation noise. In this lineage, a better marginal-likelihood fit of the accepted archive is not a guide to better candidate ranking. The decomposition shows why. Radius 3 wins on the data-fit term, not on model complexity. With amplitude fixed at 1 and noise fixed at 0.05, the model cannot otherwise explain near-identical molecules with very different scores. A larger radius makes neighbours look less alike and absorbs the clash. So the radius ends up acting as a stand-in for missing roughness or noise freedom, and the result is a flatter posterior mean that discriminates less among candidates. The molecular review fits this. On the two tasks with the largest losses, the Child's molecules drifted from what the Parent kept: on deco_hop it hung chains on a frozen core where the Parent made a ring-level change, and on sitagliptin_mpo it built dienol and thioketone chemistry where the Parent kept an intact N-aryl ring. Radius 1, by contrast, sharpened ranking where it was chosen, and its median_2 cell at 0.2418 is the first to clear the band that all 24 round-28 sibling cells sat in. That suggests a narrower follow-up: allow only the finer radius, or fit amplitude and noise jointly so the radius stops doing their job, or select by chronological ranking quality rather than likelihood. It also rules out simply turning up locality as a general fix. Still open: whether the radius-1 benefit survives on its own; whether the radius-3 harm is causal or partly path noise, since every run diverges from the first batch; and whether preferences at the edge of the menu point to radius 0 or 4. The deco_hop seed-0 cell should be read as a rare event when comparing against this Parent.
finding_summary.results: The selection ran on every one of the 435 model refits, and an independent recomputation reproduced every choice. It was far from a no-op: the inherited radius 2 won only 67 refits, against 146 for radius 1 and 222 for radius 3. Each task settled into its own pattern, closely matching what the Parent's own data would have preferred. median_2 always chose radius 1 and sitagliptin_mpo always chose radius 3; zaleplon_mpo chose radius 3 in all but one refit. drd2_docking started at radius 3 and moved to radius 2 as the archive grew, and deco_hop depended on the seed. Most choices were decisive (median margin 23 nats). The exception is the very first refit on the ten fixed starting molecules, decided by under 1 nat, which already sent every run off the Parent's path at the first batch. Everything outside the radius behaved identically. Batch sizes, pools, fallbacks, the sulfur gate and random draws were unchanged, and the first-batch candidate pools and random numbers were identical to the Parent's. Compared with the inherited radius-2 model scored on exactly the same molecules and states, the chosen model was slightly better calibrated: squared error on the scored molecules was 0.00845 against 0.00849. It ranked them slightly worse within a batch: rank correlation 0.539 against 0.548. The split follows the radius. Where radius 1 was chosen, ranking improved (median_2 0.80 vs 0.77; deco_hop 0.53 vs 0.51). Where radius 3 was chosen, it worsened (zaleplon_mpo 0.42 vs 0.47; sitagliptin_mpo 0.41 vs 0.43; drd2_docking 0.53 vs 0.56), and the spread of predicted means across the candidate pool shrank to about 0.86 of the radius-2 spread. The complete matched mean fell from 0.5965 to 0.5565, a change of -0.040 against the required +0.002. Seeds moved by -0.089, +0.021 and -0.052, and only 6 of 15 task-seed cells improved. Three cells carry the entire loss: deco_hop seed 0 (-0.221) and sitagliptin_mpo seeds 0 and 2 (-0.217, -0.169). The deco_hop cell is the Parent's rare late breakthrough to 0.856, which the Child, like every recent Child, never reached; it was actually ahead of the Parent at evaluations 200 and 250 before plateauing at 0.635. In the two sitagliptin_mpo cells the Child fell behind early (best 0.28 vs 0.51 and 0.29 vs 0.39 at evaluation 100) and never caught up. median_2, the task the brief singled out, improved modestly: mean 0.2317 vs 0.2227, with one cell at 0.2418, above every round-28 sibling cell. The other twelve cells net to roughly zero.

molecular.headline: Halogen-decorated flat heteroaromatics: one scaffold per run, N-halo amides at the top, no CF3 and no stereochemistry anywhere.
molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives the node proposed 870 optimizer molecules per task over three seeds (4350 in total; every child and parent trajectory file listed in the brief was present and readable, and context.comparison reports child_complete and paired_complete against code parent n-1744a1494180). The output is overwhelmingly ring-bearing and aromatic: per-task ring_closure_rate 0.964-0.979 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.944-0.975, RDKit mean 3.3-4.7 rings of which 1.7-4.0 are aromatic. What varies is almost entirely peripheral: a halogen, a methyl, a methoxy, or a short unsaturated chain hung on a core that was found early and then frozen. Within the top 50 of a single run the Murcko scaffold mode share reaches 0.96 and mean pairwise Morgan(2) Tanimoto reaches 0.63. Three chemical absences are uniform and checkable: not one of the 4350 proposals contains a trifluoromethyl group, no SMILES carries a formal charge (charged_rate 0.0 on every task), and no SMILES carries a stereo designation (stereocentre_rate 0.0 on every task) even though 96.7% of the molecules on one objective contain at least one unassigned stereocentre. Two chemical excesses are equally uniform: halogens land on heteroatoms as readily as on carbon (N-halogen bonds in 54.3% of one task's proposals and in 30 of its 30 highest-scoring molecules), and growth is additive and acyclic rather than ring-forming (one run's mean size rises from 42 to 86 heavy atoms, with a 117-heavy-atom proposal that is visibly one fragment duplicated). Compared with the parent on the same three seeds, this node's molecules are larger and more exotic on the two objectives where it lost most: mean 46.8 heavy atoms and 11.9 rotatable bonds versus the parent's 31.8 and 5.7 on one, and a shift from N-fluorinated aromatics to dienol/thioketone chemistry on another.

per_task.generated_character: Mid-sized flat heteroaromatics: RDKit mean 24.3 heavy atoms, MW 358, 3.3 rings of which 2.5 are aromatic, SA 3.66, mean 4.2 rotatable bonds. Every run converges on an indole- or pyrrole-2-carboxamide fused into a tricycle and capped with an N-aryl amide, most often 3-aminopyridine. In seed 1, 58% of the top 50 share the single Murcko scaffold O=C(Nc1cccnc1)c1cc2cc3ccc2n1C3; seed 0 and seed 2 converge on the same carboxamide-indole motif with mode shares 0.38 and 0.44. Decoration is methoxy, methyl, ethyl and halogen only. Best observed 0.4821 (seed 1, evaluation 257), from an initial best of 0.3051.
liabilities: all 30 highest-scoring molecules carry an N-halogen amide bond (N(F) or N(Cl)); an N-fluoroamide is an electrophilic fluorinating reagent, not a stable candidate
N-halogen bonds appear in 54.3% of all proposals here, so the exploit is systemic rather than incidental
single-atom and two-atom proposals such as C, Cl, FCl, NCl and FNF spend oracle calls and score 0.0
O-O and non-aromatic polyene rings appear at low rate (1.6% and 12.0%) and are not recoverable chemistry
missing_features: no trifluoromethyl, nitrile, or sulfonyl group in any of the 870 proposals, so the only electronic tuning available is single-atom halogen placement
no basic amine on a ring (ring basic nitrogen in 3.7% of proposals and 0 of the top 30), so no protonatable centre is ever offered
no saturated N-heterocycle fused or appended to the aromatic core (16.1% overall, 6.7% of the top 30)
no N-alkyl or N-acyl amide variants on the scoring nitrogen; the amide nitrogen is substituted only by halogen or aryl
no stereochemistry at all; stereocentre_rate 0.0 while RDKit finds a mean 0.55 unassigned stereocentres per molecule
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient rewards one fixed pharmacophore - a fused bicyclic/tricyclic indole bearing a carboxamide to a 3-pyridyl nitrogen - plus a small electron-donating substituent (OC or C) on the benzo ring. Beyond that it is flat: the 0.4821, 0.4713 and 0.4629 molecules differ only by swapping F for Cl or moving one halogen, and the two 0.4821 entries are the same molecule with F and Cl exchanged. Low scores are not wrong chemistry, they are no chemistry: the zero-scoring proposals are one- and two-atom fragments.

per_task.generated_character: The largest and least drug-like set in the node: RDKit mean 46.8 heavy atoms, MW 663, 11.9 rotatable bonds, 4.7 rings of which 4.0 aromatic, SA 4.67, and 30.6% of proposals above SA 5. The persistent core is a methylated purine-2,6-dione (xanthine-like) fused to a pyrrolo-pyridine, carrying an anilino NH with an ortho-fluorine. Everything added to it is acyclic and unsaturated: acyclic C=N imines appear in 67.7% of proposals and in 30 of the 30 highest-scoring ones, vinyl chlorides in 24.5%, O-O bonds in 16.1%. Molecules inflate during the run - seed 1 goes from a mean 42.4 heavy atoms in its first third to 85.8 in its last third, with a 117-heavy-atom proposal that is one decorated core repeated twice. Seed 0 collapsed hardest: 96% of its top 50 share one Murcko scaffold. Best observed 0.6351, first reached at evaluation 152 of seed 0 and never beaten there.
liabilities: mean MW 663 with a 117-heavy-atom proposal (CC=CC=CCc1c2c(=O)n(C)c(=N)... duplicated fragment) that no chemist would make or purify
acyclic imines on every one of the top 30 molecules; such C=N linkages hydrolyse and are usually benchmark artefacts
vinyl chloride and chloroalkyl appendages in a quarter of proposals
O-O single bonds in 16.1% of proposals
repeated identical decoration on both halves of the largest molecules, a crossover artefact rather than a design
missing_features: no ring-level replacement of the conserved linker region; the core is never swapped, only hung with chains
no amide in any of the top 30 (9.9% overall) and no sulfonamide anywhere, so the ordinary polar linkers of decoration chemistry are absent
no basic nitrogen on a ring (1.4% of proposals) and no saturated heterocyclic cap
no compact substituents: the generator adds length rather than new closed rings, leaving 11.9 rotatable bonds on average
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score is set almost entirely by the conserved fused core plus the anilino-NH link and its ortho-F; the decoration the optimizer actually explores is score-neutral. Twelve distinct molecules sit at exactly 0.6351 differing only in whether an appendage is methyl, ethyl, propyl or chloropropyl, and whether the imine sits on the aniline or on the pyridine ring. The floor is likewise structure-independent: F, C#C, CCCCC and ClCCCl all score the baseline 0.5. So the whole budget after evaluation 152 bought mass, not score. The parent, on the same seed, instead moved to a compact 31-heavy-atom pyrazolo-fused thione with a quinazolinyl N-substituent and reached 0.8561, showing that ring-level replacement rather than chain decoration is what the gradient pays for.

per_task.generated_character: The most medicinally recognisable chemistry the node produced. RDKit mean 29.8 heavy atoms, MW 443, 3.7 rings of which 1.7 aromatic and 2.0 non-aromatic, fraction sp3 carbon 0.42, SA 4.61. A basic amine is present in 90% of proposals and a ring basic nitrogen in 81.5%, rising to 100% of the top 30: the recurring unit is a 2-substituted N-alkylpyrrolidine, sometimes spiro-fused, joined by a one- to three-carbon linker to a phenol-bearing biaryl with meta F and OMe. Best observed 0.9943 (seed 1, evaluation 272) from an initial best of 0.019, the largest climb on any objective in this node.
liabilities: terminal primary alkyl chlorides on the best molecules (CCCCl, CCC(N)Cl); alkylating and metabolically unacceptable
N-vinyl pyrrolidine enamines (C=CN1CCCC1...) in the seed-0 top block; hydrolytically unstable
spiro and fused three- and four-membered rings in 20.8% of proposals, including azetidine/aziridine-like N-containing strained rings
non-aromatic rings carrying two or more double bonds in 34.0% of proposals
vinyl halides in 13.6% of proposals and 13.3% of the top 30
missing_features: no defined stereochemistry on a scoring objective that is shape-sensitive: 96.7% of proposals have at least one unassigned stereocentre and not one SMILES specifies configuration
no piperazine or piperidine ring is built de novo; the ring amine is always a pyrrolidine carried over from the initial pool and re-decorated
no amide, sulfonamide or carboxylate in the top 30, so the only polarity offered is a phenol and a primary amine
no aromatic nitrogen heterocycle paired with the basic centre; aromatic rings are carbocyclic benzenes
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient is explicit and the molecules show it: a protonatable sp3 ring nitrogen two to four atoms from an aromatic ring, a free phenol, and a second aryl ring bearing F and OMe. The 0.9943, 0.9921 and 0.9917 molecules are the same pyrrolidine-phenol-biaryl differing only in the terminal group of one propyl chain (CCl, N, C(N)Cl). Score falls away when the amine is removed: the 0.0002-0.0016 molecules are the arylsulfonyl prolinamides inherited from the initial pool, which have no basic centre at all. Late behaviour is unstable in seed 2, where the last six proposals run 0.2237-0.9143 while its best stood at 0.9143.

per_task.generated_character: Large, highly fused, nearly halogen-free polycyclics: RDKit mean 32.0 heavy atoms, MW 439, 4.5 rings of which only 2.2 aromatic, halogen in a mean 0.12 atoms per molecule (digest halogen_rate 0.109, the lowest of the five objectives), amide present in 79.3%. The recurring body is a cyclic imide or glycine-anhydride-like diketopiperazine fused onto a dibenzo or indazole system, carrying a 4-propyl, 2-ethoxy aryl head retained from early in the run. Half the proposals contain a ring of eight or more atoms (mean 0.51 per molecule) and 64.6% contain a non-aromatic ring bearing two or more double bonds. This is the most scaffold-diverse task in the node (29-32 distinct Murcko scaffolds inside a single run's top 50, 151-181 across a run) and also the lowest-scoring: best 0.2418 against an initial best of 0.1678.
liabilities: eight-plus-membered fused rings in half the proposals, a crossover artefact that produces strained and conformationally meaningless systems
acyclic N-N single bonds in 13.1% of proposals
acyclic C=N imines in 22.1% of proposals
aminal and N-CH2-N motifs inside the fused cores of the final molecules, which are hydrolytically fragile
missing_features: no second, chemically distinct pharmacophore anywhere in the set; every high scorer is one fused lactam body with the same aryl head, so a multi-target objective is being answered with one motif
a ring basic nitrogen in only 20% of the top 30 here, against 96.7% of the parent's top 30 on the same objective, so the protonatable-ring option is largely dropped
no halogenated or trifluoromethylated variants to tune lipophilicity (halogen_rate 0.109, zero CF3)
no sulfonamide (0.2%) and essentially no carboxylic acid (0.6%)
no stereochemistry written despite a mean 1.8 unassigned stereocentres per molecule
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient rewards keeping one aryl head (propyl plus ethoxy on a benzene) attached to a fused lactam/imide, and little else: the entire seed-1 top block is one scaffold varied at a single nitrogen substituent (C, CC, C=O, C(C)=O, C(=O)F), moving the score only from 0.2418 to 0.2344. Nothing the search generated moved the ceiling; the span from the best to the median molecule is 0.24 to 0.19. Molecules that drop to 0.0 are one- and two-atom fragments, so the low end again measures degenerate proposals and not informative chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: Small, heavily fluorinated, and chemically the strangest set: RDKit mean 25.4 heavy atoms, MW 370, SA 4.66 with 41.5% of proposals above SA 5, halogen present in 71.5% (digest halogen_rate 0.715). The recurring body is an N,N-dimethyl purine-2,6-dione or 2-imino-xanthine fused core onto which the search hangs partially saturated five-membered dienol rings (C3=CC(F)C=C3O) in place of an aromatic ring: non-aromatic rings with two or more double bonds occur in 72% of proposals and in 93.3% of the top 30. N-halogen bonds appear in 18.3%, O-halogen in 16.6%, and the digest records a cumulated_double_bond_rate of 0.123, the highest of the five tasks. Best observed 0.5981 (seed 1, evaluation 281) from an initial best of 0.0021.
liabilities: fluorinated thioketone (C(F)=S) on the single best molecule; a thiocarbonyl adjacent to fluorine is not an isolable motif
N-F and O-F bonds in 18.3% and 16.6% of proposals
cyclopentadienol and enol rings as aromatic surrogates, which tautomerise or oxidise immediately
O-O single bonds in 4.7% of proposals and cumulated double bonds recorded at 0.123 in the digest counters
one- and two-atom halogen and sulfur fragments (F, FF, SS, FS) consuming oracle calls at 0.0
missing_features: zero trifluoromethyl groups in all 870 proposals, and gem-difluoro in only 0.1%, while the gradient clearly pays for fluorine: fluorine arrives only one atom at a time, often on a heteroatom
no beta-amino amide or any amide at all in the top 30 (3.1% overall)
no saturated diazine ring built de novo; ring basic nitrogen is present in 18% of proposals and 20% of the top 30
no retained aromatic carbocycle on the scoring position; the search de-aromatises rings into dienols instead of substituting them
no stereochemistry, although the fused cores it writes have a mean 1.1 unassigned stereocentres
per_task.score_gradient_reading: More fluorine plus more hydrogen-bonding NH/OH on the same bicyclic core raises the score. The top molecule adds a fluorinated thioketone chain and a fluorinated dienol ring to the imino-xanthine; the 0.5539, 0.5364 and 0.5212 molecules are the same core with the chain shortened or the F count changed. The low end is again degenerate: F, FF, SS and FS all score 0.0. The run ends far below its own best, with seed 2's last six proposals at 0.0-0.2925, so what the search retained late is not what scored. On the same seeds the parent kept an intact N-aryl ring and a higher N-fluorination rate in its top block (80% versus 20% here) and reached 0.6943.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Not one of the 4350 optimizer proposals across all objectives and all three seeds contains a trifluoromethyl group, and geminal difluoro carbons appear in at most 2.3% of any objective's proposals. Yet on the two objectives where halogen content is highest (digest halogen_rate 0.840 and 0.715) the highest-scoring molecules carry 1.7-2.3 halogens each, added one atom at a time.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot assemble a polyfluorinated carbon centre; it only places single halogen atoms.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Mutation is atom-local, so a motif that needs three halogens on one carbon requires three independently accepted edits and is effectively unreachable. The generator needs group-level substituent insertion, where a whole small functional group is attached or replaced as one move, rather than only single-atom identity changes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: N-halogen bonds occur in 54.3% of one objective's proposals and in 30 of its 30 highest-scoring molecules, for example CCc1c2c(OC)cc3c1cc(C(=O)N(F)c1cccnc1)n3C2(C)F and CCc1c2c(OC)cc3c1cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c1cccnc1)n3C2C, which are N-halo amides. O-halogen bonds reach 16.6% and O-O single bonds 16.1% on other objectives, and thiocarbonyl-fluoride appears on a top molecule, Cn1c(=N)c2c(CC(F)C(F)=S)n(C3=CC(F)C=C3O)cc2n(C)c1=O.
transferable_gaps.gap: Halogens and other substituents are placed on heteroatoms as readily as on carbon, producing valence-legal but chemically unstable bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The atom-mutation operator uses a valence check with no bonding-context rule. A task-agnostic generator should restrict halogen attachment to carbon and reject heteroatom-heteroatom single bonds formed by mutation, so that scoring improvements are bought with chemistry a chemist could keep.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Where the starting molecules contained a pyrrolidine, a ring basic nitrogen appears in 81.5% of proposals and in 100% of the top 30, and the highest-scoring molecule of the whole node, CCCN1CCCC1(CN)c1cc(-c2cc(F)cc(OC)c2)c(O)cc1CCCCl, is built around it. Where the pool did not supply one, ring basic nitrogen falls to 1.4-3.7% of proposals and 0-20% of the top 30, and no run recovers it.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot create a new saturated nitrogen heterocycle; it can only re-decorate basic-amine rings that the initial pool already supplied.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring formation in the operator set is limited to fusing or closing onto existing ring atoms, so a saturated amine ring is never introduced where one is absent. The generator needs ring-insertion moves that can graft a small saturated heterocycle onto an acyclic or aromatic position, independent of what the starting population contained.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one objective the proposals average 46.8 heavy atoms, MW 663 and 11.9 rotatable bonds, against the code parent's 31.8 heavy atoms and 5.7 rotatable bonds on the identical seeds, and within one run the mean rises from 42.4 heavy atoms in the first third to 85.8 in the last. The largest proposal has 117 heavy atoms and is one decorated core duplicated verbatim.
transferable_gaps.gap: Growth is additive and acyclic: the generator extends chains rather than closing rings, so molecules inflate in mass without gaining structure.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Crossover concatenates fragments with no size control and mutation only appends, so molecular mass is an unbounded free parameter. The generator needs a size or rotatable-bond penalty on offspring acceptance, plus a ring-closing move so that added atoms buy new ring systems instead of floppy chains.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Inside a single run's top 50 the Murcko scaffold mode share reaches 0.96 and the mean pairwise Morgan(2) Tanimoto reaches 0.63; one plateau contains twelve distinct molecules at identical score differing only in whether an appendage is methyl, ethyl, propyl or chloropropyl. On another objective the first twelve ranked molecules are one scaffold varied at a single nitrogen substituent across a score range of 0.0074.
transferable_gaps.gap: Once a core scores, the generator stops changing it: whole runs collapse onto one scaffold and only permute peripheral atoms.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Selection concentrates breeding on the current best structure and the operators available to it are peripheral, so the population loses scaffold variety long before the budget ends. The generator needs either scaffold-level moves (core replacement, ring-size change, ring-system hopping) or an explicit structural-novelty term in parent selection.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Proposals such as C, Cl, FCl, NCl, FNF, FF, SS, OCS, C#C, ClCl and CCCCC appear in every objective, 3-12 times per 290-proposal run, and score at the floor of their objective (0.0 on three objectives, the 0.5 baseline on another).
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits degenerate one- and two-atom fragments that consume evaluations and carry no chemical information.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Deletion and fragment-selection moves can reduce a molecule to a stub with no lower bound, and nothing filters the result before it is scored. A minimum heavy-atom count and a rejection of offspring that lose a ring system entirely would return those evaluations to the search at no modelling cost.

transferable_gaps.evidence: stereocentre_rate is 0.0 and charged_rate is 0.0 in the digest counters for every objective and every seed, while RDKit finds a mean 2.59 unassigned stereocentres per molecule on one objective, where 96.7% of proposals have at least one.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never writes stereochemistry or formal charge, so two whole axes of molecular variation are outside its reach.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: SMILES are emitted flat, so enantiomers and diastereomers are indistinguishable to the optimizer and a scoring function sensitive to three-dimensional fit or to ionisation state cannot be optimised against. A task-agnostic generator should be able to set or invert a stereocentre and to propose ionisable or zwitterionic forms as ordinary moves.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Non-aromatic rings bearing two or more double bonds reach 72.0% of proposals and 93.3% of the top 30 on one objective, where aromatic rings are replaced by fluorinated cyclopentadienols such as the C3=CC(F)C=C3O unit of Cn1c(=N)c2c(CC(F)C(F)=S)n(C3=CC(F)C=C3O)cc2n(C)c1=O; on another, half the proposals contain a ring of eight or more atoms, with aminal N-CH2-N bridges inside the fused cores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator de-aromatises rings and builds oversized fused systems instead of substituting on intact aromatic rings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Bond-order and ring-fusion mutations are applied without any aromaticity or ring-size constraint, so the search drifts into tautomerically unstable dienols and strained medium rings that cannot be made. Constrain bond-order edits to preserve aromatic rings, and bound the ring size that fusion moves may create.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
